newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai soymeal quiet, buyers expect lower prices.
newsitem.headline: Thai soymeal quiet, buyers expect lower prices.

text.p: Thai grain trade activity has remained moderate this week as buyers stay on the sidelines in anticipation of further price falls, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Except for the recent purchase of 50,000 tonnes of soybeans by oil crushers for January shipment, there have been no new buying orders, they said.
Market talk put the price for the purchase at $291-295 c&f Bangkok, but crusher sources declined to comment.
One major feed producer was said to have sought a cargo of soymeal for prompt shipment at $300 a tonne c&f Bangkok.
"But no deal was made because the prices were quoted by traders above that level," a trader said.
U.S.-origin soymeal for January shipment was quoted at around $318 a tonne c&f Bangkok, while Indian origin was quoted at about $308 on the same basis, according to trade sources.
"The supply at the moment is enough to cover this year's demand. Buyers are not under pressure to buy. I believe if soybean prices dropped a bit further, buyers would emerge," said another trader.

Although local soymeal stocks were diminishing, prices eased as an influx of imported product pulled them down. Prices of local soymeal were quoted at around 9.20-9.50 baht ($0.36) a kg from 9.60 baht last week.
"The removal of the import quota on soybean and soymeal which went into effect on November 1 also pressured the prices," another importer said.
Corn prices were steady to lower at 4.28-4.40 baht per kg from 4.30-4.40 baht last week as some feed producers and poultry farmers turned to cheaper broken rice as a substitute.

On the local supply side, the agriculture ministry was likely to keep its estimate of 1996/97 output of soybean (April-March) and corn (July-June) unchanged from its previous forecast at 352,600 tonnes and 4.38 million tonnes respectively, according to a senior ministry source.
The new forecast is expected to be released in early December.
